newsitem.title: UK: BG plc signs Trinidad gas production sharing deal.
newsitem.headline: BG plc signs Trinidad gas production sharing deal.

text.p: A consortium of BG plc, Agip SpA of Italy and Deminex of Germany have signed a production sharing contract with the government of Trinidad and Tobago to open a new offshore hydrocarbon province off the north coast of Trinidad, BG said in a statement on Thursday.
The North Coast Marine Area contains four undeveloped gas fields, Hibiscus, Orchid, Iris and Poinsettia, with potential reserves of over 3 trillion cubic feet.

BG will be the consortium's operator, and the group will carry out immediate exploration in the 230,000 acre area which lies 40 km offshore. Two exploration wells will be drilled in the next six months.

The market for the gas will be the Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) plant of Atlantic LNG Company of Trinidad and Tobago at Point Fortin. BG holds a 26 percent shareholding in the company, whose $1 billion plant is due on stream in winter 1998/9.

The contract was signed in Port of Spain on Wednesday, and will have an exploration period of six years from the date of signing. There is an option to move into a development phase for the following 25 years.

BG currently supplies 164 million cubic feet a day of natural gas to the National Gas Company of Trinidad and Tobago from the offshore Dolphin field. BG is Dolphin's operator and 50 percent partner with Texaco.
